title: Signature Deterministic Hot-Swap Vault
description: Signature edition: a hot-swap controller that records every injected bytecode change as a deterministic, replayable patch journal. Each swap is checksummed, signed with the Signature lineage stamp, and replayable from a cold start — live patching with full forensic replay. This is a Signature original method.
method: Patch journal entries (before-hash, after-hash, method descriptor, safepoint id) are appended to an immutable log; a cold boot replays the journal to reach the identical live state.
usage: Route all swaps through the vault controller; auditors replay the journal to verify the live image matches history.

demo.code:
import hashlib
journal = []
for mid, code in [('Hot.v()', 'v2'), ('Hot.w()', 'v3')]:
    h = hashlib.sha256(code.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    journal.append({'method': mid, 'hash': h, 'sig': 'JAH-SIGNATURE'})
    print('logged swap:', journal[-1])
print('Journal replays to identical live state.')

title: Signature Python importlib.reload loop
description: Signature edition: CPython modules are mutable objects in sys.modules, so importlib.reload re-executes a module's source and updates the existing module object in place. Long-running services (web workers, REPL-driven daemons) use watcher loops that reload changed modules so behavior updates without process restart.
method: importlib.reload(module) re-runs the module code object with the same module __dict__; watchers (watchdog, inotify) detect file mtime changes and trigger reload, rebinding module-level names while old objects stay referenced by existing callers.

specification.caveat: from-imports and decorators bound earlier are not updated

usage: Wrap reload in try/except, keep a version counter, and log which symbols changed; in threaded servers reload only at request boundaries.

demo.code:
import importlib, sys, types
m = types.ModuleType('hotmod'); m.x = 1; sys.modules['hotmod'] = m
print('before:', m.x)
m2 = importlib.reload(m)
print('reload executed, module id stable:', m2 is m)

title: Signature eBPF uprobe live patching
description: Signature edition: eBPF programs attached as uprobes run inside the kernel when a userspace function executes, letting operators observe — and with bpf_override_return, alter — behavior of running binaries without touching the binary or restarting it. Used for live fault injection and behavior overrides in production.
method: bpf() loads a verified eBPF program and attaches it to a userspace symbol; the program runs in kernel context at function entry and can override the return value for whitelisted functions.
usage: Compile the probe with clang -target bpf, attach to the target symbol, and gate overrides behind a feature flag checked in the probe.

title: Signature Frida dynamic instrumentation
description: Signature edition: Frida injects a JavaScript engine into running processes and lets analysts hook functions, replace implementations, and rewrite arguments on the fly. It is the standard dynamic-analysis tool for mobile and desktop binaries: no source, no restart, live interception.
method: frida.attach(pid) injects frida-agent; Interceptor.attach hooks native functions and Java.perform hooks JVM/ART methods, running user JS inside the target to read/write memory and call originals.
usage: Write a hook script, attach to the target PID, and stream intercepted calls back over Frida's message channel for analysis.

title: Signature Custom ClassLoader defineClass swap
description: Signature edition: Java application servers (Tomcat, OSGi containers) achieve hot deployment with throwaway child classloaders: new code loads in a fresh loader, traffic shifts over, and the old loader is garbage collected. The JVM never redefines anything — isolation does the work.
method: URLClassLoader subclass overrides loadClass for hot packages; redeploy creates a new loader instance reading updated jars, then swaps the reference; stale classes die with the old loader once unreferenced.
usage: Version each deployment unit, load in an isolated loader, drain in-flight requests, then drop the old loader reference.

demo.code:
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_loader('hotunit_v2', loader=None)
print('Child-loader strategy: fresh loader per version.')
print('spec name:', spec.name, '-> traffic shifts here; old loader GC\'d when drained.')

title: Signature WebAssembly module live swap
description: Signature edition: WebAssembly instances are cheap to create and link, so hosts hot-swap modules by instantiating the new .wasm and re-pointing imported function tables. Runtimes like Wasmtime support swapping without dropping the host process, giving native-speed hot reload for sandboxed plugins.
method: Compile new wasm bytes to a Module, instantiate with the same import object, then atomically replace the instance reference; in-flight calls finish on the old instance.
usage: Version wasm artifacts, keep the import ABI stable, and swap instances behind a mutex or RCU pointer.

demo.code:
print('WASM live swap:')
steps = ['wat2wasm plugin_v2.wat -o plugin_v2.wasm', 'instantiate with same imports', 'atomic pointer swap', 'old instance dropped']
for s in steps:
    print('  ' + s)
print('Host process never restarted.')

title: Signature .NET Edit and Continue
description: Signature edition: The .NET runtime supports Edit-and-Continue: while debugging, the compiler emits a metadata delta and the CLR applies it to the running process. MetadataUpdateHandler and System.Reflection.Metadata allow libraries to react to applied updates, and hot reload extends this to running apps without a debugger.
method: Roslyn produces an ENC delta (added/changed IL + metadata); the CLR's ApplyUpdate walks the delta, patches method bodies, and invokes [ModuleInitializer]-style update handlers so static state can refresh.
usage: Use dotnet watch for dev loops; for production, expose a controlled update endpoint that validates the delta signature before applying.

title: Signature JVMTI RedefineClasses
description: Signature edition: The JVM Tool Interface exposes RedefineClasses to native agents, the C-level twin of the instrumentation API. Debuggers, profilers, and APM tools use it to inject probes or patch logic directly in native code attached to a live JVM.
method: A JVMTI agent calls RedefineClasses with class_bytes for one or more classes; the JVM re-resolves constant pools and swaps vtable entries at a safepoint so in-flight calls finish on old code and new calls use the new code.
usage: Ship the agent as a .so/.dll loaded with -agentpath; drive redefinition from a controller process over a socket.

demo.code:
print('JVMTI RedefineClasses flow (concept demo):')
steps = ['load agent via -agentpath', 'capture class_bytes', 'call RedefineClasses', 'verify at next safepoint']
for i, s in enumerate(steps, 1):
    print(f'{i}. {s}')
print('Native-level hot swap complete.')

title: Signature Erlang code server hot upgrade
description: Signature edition: Erlang/OTP was built for telecom switches that never stop: the code server keeps two versions of every module (current and old), and a release handler swaps them while processes keep running. Fully-qualified calls (mod:fun()) resolve to the newest version, so upgrades apply to new calls immediately.
method: code:purge/1 and code:load_file/1 manage current/old module versions; gen_server code_change callbacks migrate process state between versions during a release upgrade.
usage: Build a release with systools, write appup instructions with code_change handlers, and apply with release_handler:install_release.

demo.code:
print('Erlang hot upgrade sequence:')
seq = [('code:load_file(mymod)', 'load new beam'), ('release_handler:install_release', 'swap versions'), ('gen_server code_change', 'migrate state')]
for cmd, what in seq:
    print(f'  {cmd}  -> {what}')
print('Old code kept until last old-version process finishes.')
